County codes and joins

Source: vignettes/county-data.Rmd
county-data.Rmd
library(knbsdata)

County-level work in Kenya lives or dies on join keys. This vignette covers the reference codes knbs_geographies() provides, the two mistakes that silently corrupt county joins, and what this package deliberately does not offer.

Chunks that contact the service are shown but not run.

The reference 

geo <- knbs_geographies()
counties <- knbs_geographies(level = "county")
mombasa_subs <- knbs_geographies(parent = "01")

One row per territorial unit of the 2019 Population and Housing Census frame: Kenya ("00"), 47 counties ("01"–"47"), and their sub-counties (four digits, the first two being the county). Names, levels and parent codes come with it, read live from the census service (CC BY 4.0) rather than shipped as a snapshot that could drift from the source.

The two classic corruptions

Leading zeros. County codes are character, and "01" is not 1. The moment a code passes through as.numeric() — or through a CSV round-trip that guesses types — Mombasa ("01") collides with nothing and matches nothing. Everything in this package keeps codes as character; keep them that way in your own pipelines, and if you read codes from a file, read that column as character explicitly.

Vintage mixing. These are the 2019 census frame units. Administrative units change: joining 2019 codes against a table coded to another frame will drop or misassign rows without erroring. The vintage column exists so that the frame travels with the data; check it before joining anything that did not come from this package.

A worked join

County population against the reference, giving each county its share:

pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
totals <- pop[pop$sex == "total" & pop$marital_status == "Total",
              c("geo_code", "geo_name", "value")]

geo <- knbs_geographies(level = "county")
joined <- merge(totals, geo[, c("geo_code", "parent_code")], by = "geo_code")

joined$share <- joined$value / sum(joined$value)
head(joined[order(-joined$share), ])

The join is exact by construction: observations and reference use the same codes from the same source.

Gross County Product

The county economy itself is served by the Open Data for Africa republisher (source_id "opendataforafrica"), the one source that carries GCP as data: GVA shares plus constant- and current-price GCP for all 47 counties, annual 2013–2020.

gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")
latest <- gcp[gcp$table_code == "T3" & gcp$period == 2020 & gcp$geo_code != "KE", ]
head(latest[order(-latest$value), c("geo_name", "value")])

Two cautions, both stated in knbs_metadata(): this is the 2021 edition — newer GCP years exist only as PDF reports (knbs_publications("gross county product")) — and its geography codes are the portal’s own region codes, not census territories. To relate GCP to census-coded data, translate its county names into census codes with knbs_county_code(), as below, rather than joining on its region codes.

Matching county names across sources

County names are not spelled alike even within KNBS: the census writes “Murang’a”, “Tharaka-Nithi” and “Nairobi City”, the Data Portal “MURANGA”, “THARAKA NITHI” and “NAIROBI”, under codes of its own (KE_200_MU). Treasury, Controller of Budget and survey data add their own variants. knbs_county_code() turns any of them into the census codes:

knbs_county_code(c("Murang'a", "MURANGA", "Nairobi City County",
                   "taita/taveta", "Homabay", "47"))
#> [1] "21" "21" "47" "06" "43" "47"

Matching sets aside case, punctuation, spacing, apostrophes and the words “County”, “City” and “Government”; numbers 1 to 47 are county numbers; “Kenya” is "00". Nothing else is matched — there is no list of alternative names to guess from — so a misspelling becomes NA with a warning that names it and suggests the nearest official name:

knbs_county_code("Kakamenga")
#> Warning: 1 value matched no county and became `NA`:
#> • "Kakamenga" (did you mean "Kakamega"?)

knbs_match_counties(c("Kakamenga", "Uasin-Gishu", "07"))   # how each matched

That makes cross-source joins one line. The rural share of each county’s population, from the Data Portal’s rural table and the census:

library(dplyr)

rural <- knbs_get_indicator("DF_POP_CENSUS_RUR", source = "knbs_opendata") |>
  filter(indic_phc_code == "POP_TOT", sex == "total", geo_code != "KE") |>
  mutate(county_code = knbs_county_code(geo_name))     # "MURANGA" -> "21"

total <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0002", geo_level = "county") |>
  filter(sex == "total", age_type == "total")

rural |>
  inner_join(total, by = c(county_code = "geo_code"),
             suffix = c("_rural", "_total")) |>
  mutate(rural_share = value_rural / value_total) |>
  arrange(desc(rural_share))
#> Bomet 0.97, Kitui 0.96, Elgeyo/Marakwet 0.96, ... Kiambu 0.30;
#> Nairobi City and Mombasa NA: the portal reports no rural population there.

All 48 names the portal uses (47 counties and KENYA) match, to 48 distinct codes.

What is deliberately absent

  • Other vintages and crosswalks. Only the 2019 frame has a verified source. knbs_geographies(vintage = 2009) fails with a clear error rather than serving an unverified concordance — a wrong crosswalk is worse than none.
  • Boundaries. knbs_boundaries() does not exist. No officially licensed, redistributable boundary file has been verified, and the plan implements boundaries only after that review.
  • Classifications. Industry, occupation and product classifications have no audited source yet.

If you know an official source for any of these, a data source change issue is the right place to point at it.
